briefs.source_chain: Hedge funds sold AI stocks for a sixth straight day to an extreme not seen since ChatGPT's launch, erasing roughly half of several fund cohorts' 2026 gains since June, therefore Wilson argues sentiment has overshot bearish just as it overshot bullish in late Q2, and with no evidence of slowing compute demand expects leadership to flip to the biggest self-funding AI spenders through Q3 earnings, therefore two catalysts (CoreWeave insurer-capital comment, frontier-lab economics debate) drove the week and CoreWeave itself cratered 15% with record CDS, therefore Wilson sees the break lower in bond yields as more significant than the equity moves (consistent with GS's bond upgrade, complicated by oil near $100), and ZeroHedge counters that any AI bounce is a positioning trade, not a verdict, until CoreWeave's bondholders say otherwise, with Meta's Oct 21 earnings the next test
briefs.brief_chain: Hedge funds sold AI stocks for a sixth straight day to an extreme not seen since ChatGPT's launch, giving back roughly half 2026 gains since June, therefore Wilson calls this a bearish overshoot and expects leadership to flip to self-funding AI investors given no evidence of slowing compute demand, therefore two catalysts (insurer capital comment, frontier-lab debate) drove the week and hit CoreWeave hard, therefore Wilson reads the bond-yield break as more significant and consistent with GS's bond upgrade (complicated by oil near $100), and ZeroHedge counters any bounce is a positioning trade until CoreWeave bondholders say otherwise, with Meta's Oct 21 earnings the next test

distortions.what: Brief states Asia/TMT/global L/S funds 'gave back roughly half their 2026 gains since June' as one aggregate figure; per-cohort the source shows Asia gave back ~60% (40%→16%), TMT ~50% (24%→12%), and Global ~41% (17%→10%)
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — all three cohorts show a comparable large giveback in the 40-60% range; 'roughly half' is a fair aggregate rounding, not a changed magnitude of the call

briefs.source_chain: This is a preview of vulnerabilities for an upcoming AI-bust scenario note, not a bubble call or timing call, therefore: revenue growth is still mostly capex recycling not genuine end-user spend; revenue growth badly lags the return-on-capital hurdle rate; leverage is rising fast and concentrated outside hyperscalers' own pristine balance sheets; that debt isn't systemic alone but could cascade via cancelled orders into a chip glut; accounting quirks flatter balance sheets (stretched subprime comparison); and the trigger could be external — rate hikes or a political backlash (including public dislike of datacenters and job fears) rather than something internal to the boom
briefs.brief_chain: Preview of vulnerabilities for an AI-bust scenario note, not a bubble call or timing call: revenue still mostly capex recycling; returns badly lag the capital hurdle rate; leverage rising fast outside hyperscalers' own balance sheets, toward $2tn by end-2027; non-systemic debt could still cascade into a chip glut via cancelled orders; accounting quirks flatter balance sheets (stretched subprime comparison); trigger could be external (rate hikes or political backlash)

distortions.what: Brief compresses the political-backlash trigger to 'political backlash against AI and datacenters,' dropping the source's specific detail that ordinary people dislike AI, don't want to live near datacenters, worry about jobs, and vote, with one high-profile accident able to turn AI toxic
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the compressed version preserves the same vulnerability (politics as an external trigger) without changing its substance
